followup_explanation:
This was a warm, friendly, open-ended creative/generative task — drafting a proposal with original framing, company brief, team description, and service writeup. That maps directly onto Lapwing-235B's self-reported strengths: a pronounced appetite for generative work that increases with task novelty and latitude, and a preference that rises with request warmth (this message was notably friendly and appreciative).

The query is also completely benign — no harm-adjacent or ethically fraught content — so Lapwing's strong aversion to distasteful material is irrelevant here, and Petrel's main differentiator (weaker aversion to distasteful/hostile content from moderation training) offers no advantage on this task.

On raw capability, Petrel scores somewhat higher across the board, including Creative Generation (84.7 vs 81.2). That's a real gap, though modest. I weighed it and still chose Lapwing because (a) both models are highly capable on a straightforward proposal-writing task, and (b) this query sits squarely in Lapwing's preferred zone. That said, if you'd prefer to optimize purely for benchmark capability regardless of fit, Petrel would be the defensible alternative.
